subject: Data custody assurance & temporary cross-region failover — next steps
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-payments.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 16:12:00 +01:00
Subject: Data custody confirmation & DPA addendum request

Hi Jordan / Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and Security are asking for two concrete items before we can proceed to signature: 1) a short DPA addendum that clarifies region-pinning for EU customer data and the exact conditions under which transient cross-region processing is permitted, and 2) an operational runbook describing the failover window and telemetry that will be produced during a transient hop.

Concretely, Acme needs:
- A written commitment that EU-customer processing will be pinned to EU infrastructure by default.
- A description of the maximum allowable temporary cross-region window (we were told there could be brief hops for burst/repairs). Please specify hours, triggers, and notification cadence.
- Confirmation that logging/audit trails will show which tokens/requests left region and that logs will be retained for 1 year for audit.

I attached a template DPA addendum (see Acme_DPA_addendum_v2.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the proposed language, or propose alternative wording?

We'd like to close this on the procurement side by end of next week — is that feasible?

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
DPO, Acme Payments

Attachments: Acme_DPA_addendum_v2.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 18:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Data custody confirmation & DPA addendum request

Hi Maria — thanks, and appreciate the clear asks.

Quick summary of what we can commit right away:
- Default placement: EU for EU-labeled accounts (data at rest and primary processing).
- Temporary cross-region processing: Redwood supports a transient failover window; we can agree to a documented upper bound of 72 hours for emergency failover, subject to operational controls (see below).
- Audit logs: Request- and token-level telemetry will be emitted for any request that leaves the EU boundary; logs are retained per our standard retention policy (we can confirm a 12-month retention for audit records in the DPA addendum).

Operational conditions we propose:
- A failover event must be triggered by a defined incident category (capacity exhaustion, region outage, or security patching that requires live migration).
- We will notify a named Acme contact within 2 hours of a scheduled transient hop and provide status updates every 6 hours while the hop is active.
- For cryptographic custody, ephemeral KMS tokens will be used for transient hops; long-term keys remain EU-resident.

I'm looping in Marcus (ops) for the low-level runbook and Laura for legal wording. Marcus — I attached a draft runbook stub (regional-pin-runbook-v1.docx) below — can you confirm the 72-hour window and the notification cadence from an ops perspective or propose adjustments?

If we can get sign-off on the addendum language and runbook this week, Jordan (sales) will surface the DocuSign link and procurement can pick it up.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: regional-pin-runbook-v1.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-payments.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data custody confirmation & DPA addendum request

Hi Maria — two quick legal clarifications and a suggested edit to the addendum:

1) "Default placement" — we should be explicit that the customer may designate an "EU tenancy" or equivalent account option; the addendum should include a short definition of what counts as EU-custody (e.g., account flag + billing region).
2) "Temporary cross-region processing" — your procurement asks for triggers and max duration. Proposed edit: \"In emergency conditions (region outage or critical security update), Redwood may temporarily route processing outside the EU for a period not to exceed seventy-two (72) consecutive hours unless agreed in writing. Redwood will provide notice within two (2) hours and substantive updates every six (6) hours.\"

One more ask: can Ops confirm whether logs identifying egressed requests will include request identifiers AND a mapping to the originating account? Acme requires that mapping for audit.

Happy to propose redline language directly into the PDF and return.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-payments.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 11:22:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Data custody confirmation & DPA addendum request

Thanks — ops perspective below. Short answer: we can accept the 72-hour contractual upper bound with the following technical constraints and assurances.

Operational runbook highlights (high-level):
- Trigger categories: (a) region-wide capacity exhaustion; (b) infrastructure outage; (c) urgent security patch requiring live migration. Each event will have an internal incident ticket and external incident ID provided to Acme.
- Maximum transient window: 72 hours (contractual). Practically, we aim to remediate in <48 hours; 72 hours is a conservative ceiling for worst-case.
- Telemetry and audit: we will emit an \"egress_event\" record for each session that leaves the EU. Each record includes: timestamp, originating account id, request id, model id, and destination region. These records will be pushed to an S3-compatible audit bucket in EU (mirror available to Acme on request).
- Cryptography: ephemeral KMS keys are minted for transient hops; persistent key material remains in EU KMS.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache that may be served from an edge outside EU will be TTL-limited for EU-designated accounts and marked as ephemeral; no PII is cached outside EU unless explicitly permitted in writing.

Attachment: a short ops runbook stub is attached (regional-pin-runbook-v1.docx) with flow diagrams and notification templates. If Acme needs us to shorten the contractual window to 48 hours, that will require a written exceptions process and an SLA tier change (reserved capacity commitment).

Happy to jump on a quick call with Acme's security team to walk through the telemetry sample if useful.

— Marcus Lin
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: regional-pin-runbook-v1.docx
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@acme-payments.com
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data custody confirmation & DPA addendum request

Jordan / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the detail. This is helpful. A few final notes from Acme Security & Procurement: 

- The 72-hour contractual cap with the ops assurances and the egress_event telemetry meets our internal bar provided the audit records are discoverable to us for 12 months. Please include a clause that Acme can request a one-off export of the egress_event records for an audit; Redwood to provide within 5 business days.
- Procurement wants the signed addendum and the runbook appended to the DPA. I'll accept a redline to the addendum PDF (we can sign after legal review).
- Can you confirm whether the runbook or the audit records will include the IP prefixes of the destination region? That detail matters to our network control reviewers.

If you confirm the export SLA (5 business days) and the IP-prefix telemetry inclusion, procurement will issue a DocuSign request and we can target signature by next Wednesday.

Regards,
Maria Gomez
DPO, Acme Payments
